sub: Named after al-Aʿlā, “the Most High”, in ayah 1
theme: Glorify Allah, who creates, shapes and guides everything. The Prophet ﷺ is promised he won’t forget the revelation and is told to remind. Success belongs to whoever purifies himself and prays, because the Hereafter lasts.
story: One of the earliest surahs, revealed in Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ was not yet used to receiving revelation and feared forgetting its words, so he would repeat them before Jibrīl had finished.
The surah reassures him: Allah will make him recite, and he will not forget. His task is only to remind. Those who fear Allah will listen; the most wretched will turn away.
The Prophet ﷺ recited it with Al-Ghāshiyah in the Eid and Friday prayers, and named it to Muʿādh as the kind of surah to recite when leading prayer.

sections.title: Glorify your Lord, the Most High
sections.meaning: Declare the perfection of your Lord’s name, the Most High. He created and gave everything its right shape, set a measure for everything and guided it, brought out green pasture, and then turned it into dark, dry stubble.
points: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
Who brings out pasture, then makes it dark stubble
sections.matters: It opens with tawḥīd in one sentence: remember Allah only in ways that befit Him. Then it shows why: every creature’s design, purpose and life cycle come from Him.
sections.story: No specific incident. When the Prophet ﷺ recited ayah 1 he would say “Subḥāna rabbiyal-aʿlā”, and he told Muslims to say it in their prostrations.
explained: Sabbiḥ: declare Allah free of every flaw, and use His name with respect, only as He named Himself. Al-Aʿlā: the Most High. He khalaqa, created from nothing, then sawwā, gave each thing a balanced form.

Qaddara: He set a measure and purpose for everything, then hadā, guided each creature to it: the animal to its pasture, the person to the paths of good and evil. He brings out green pasture, then turns it into ghuthāʾ aḥwā, dark dry stubble, a reminder that bodies fade too.
teaches: Say Subḥāna rabbiyal-aʿlā in sujūd, as the Prophet ﷺ taught.
Speak of Allah only with names that befit Him.
Everything was made for a purpose and guided to it.
Green today, dry tomorrow: life in this world fades.
sections.hook: Three “alladhī” (Who) lines in a row: 2, 3, 4. Each pairs two actions: created → proportioned, measured → guided, brought out → made stubble.

sections.title: We will make you recite; so remind
sections.meaning: Allah promises the Prophet ﷺ: We will make you recite and you will not forget, except what Allah wills, and We will ease you toward ease. So remind. Whoever fears Allah takes the reminder. The most wretched avoid it and burn in the greatest Fire, neither dying nor living.
points: You will recite and not forget, except what Allah wills
We will ease you toward ease
So remind, if the reminder benefits
Whoever fears Allah will take heed
The wretched avoid it: the great Fire, neither dying nor living
sections.matters: It frees the Prophet ﷺ from two worries: forgetting the revelation, and forcing people to believe. His job is to receive and to remind. The listeners then sort themselves into two groups.
sections.story: The Prophet ﷺ used to repeat the words before Jibrīl finished, fearing he would forget, and ayah 6 was revealed. Reportedly ayah 10 refers to Ibn Umm Maktūm, and ayah 11 to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah.
explained: Sanuqriʾuka: We will make you recite, so you will not forget. The only exception is what Allah wills, such as ayat He chose to remove. He knows what is said aloud and what is hidden. Nuyassiruka lil-yusrā: He makes good deeds easy for him and gives him an easy, straight law.

So remind, wherever the reminder benefits. The one who fears Allah and knows he will meet Him will take it. The ashqā, the most wretched, steers clear of it. He enters the greatest Fire, where he neither dies and rests, nor lives a life worth living.
teaches: The Quran’s preservation is Allah’s gift, not human skill.
Allah made His religion easy; receive it that way.
Keep reminding; the one who fears Allah will benefit.
Fear of Allah opens the heart to advice.
sections.hook: The Prophet ﷺ is told “you will not forget” (6); the wretched one “will neither die nor live” (13). The page turns at ayah 11, where the wretched one appears.

sections.title: Success: purify yourself and pray
sections.meaning: Whoever purifies himself, remembers his Lord’s name and prays has truly succeeded. But you prefer this life, while the Hereafter is better and lasts forever. This same message was in the earliest scriptures, those of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.
points: Remembers his Lord’s name and prays
You prefer this world; the Hereafter is better and lasting
Also in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā
sections.matters: It sums up the whole path in three steps and names the real obstacle: preferring what is near over what lasts. And it shows this is not a new message but the old message of the prophets.
sections.story: No agreed incident. Some reports link ayat 14–15 to charity before the Eid prayer, though the surah is Makkan. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly told Abū Dharr that these ayat were in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.
explained: Tazakkā: he purified himself from shirk, wrongdoing and bad character; some include purifying his wealth. Then he remembers his Lord’s name, until it fills his heart, and he prays. That is falāḥ, true success.

But people prefer the dunyā because it is right in front of them, while the Hereafter is only described. Yet the Hereafter is khayr, better in every way, and abqā, lasting. No wise person trades a moment’s pleasure for lasting regret. This was already written in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.
teaches: Purify the heart; remembrance and prayer grow from it.
Choose what lasts over what is merely close.
Putting this world before the Hereafter is at the root of many wrongs.
The core message never changed, from Ibrāhīm and Mūsā to Muḥammad ﷺ.
sections.hook: Three verbs in 14–15: tazakkā, dhakara, ṣallā. Khayrun wa abqā (17) contrasts with the fading pasture of ayah 5. Two prophets close the surah: Ibrāhīm, then Mūsā.

groups.text: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.
He created and proportioned, measured and guided.
He brings out green pasture, then turns it into dark, dry stubble.
We will make you recite and you won’t forget, except what Allah wills. He knows the open and hidden.
We will ease you toward the easy way.
So remind; whoever fears Allah will take the reminder.
The most wretched avoid it, and burn in the great Fire, neither dying nor living.
Successful is whoever purifies himself, remembers his Lord’s name and prays.
You prefer this world, but the Hereafter is better and lasts.
This is in the earliest scriptures, those of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.

1.explain: Sabbiḥ: declare His perfection. Ism is His name, kept pure, or Allah Himself. On reciting it, say “Subḥāna rabbiyal-aʿlā”; the Prophet ﷺ told Muslims to say this in sujūd.

2.explain: Khalaqa fa-sawwā: He created everything and made it well-balanced, every limb and part suited to its purpose.

3.explain: Qaddara fa-hadā: He set a measure and destiny for everything, then guided each creature to it: animals to their pastures, people to the paths of good and evil.

4.explain: He brings out al-marʿā, the pasture: every kind of plant that people and animals feed on.

5.explain: Then He turns it into ghuthāʾ, dry broken stubble, aḥwā, dark after being green. Only He brings both spring and decay.

6.explain: Sanuqriʾuka: We will make you recite the Quran, and you will not forget it. A great promise to the Prophet ﷺ, who could not read or write.
6.why: He used to repeat the start of an ayah before Jibrīl had finished it, fearing he would forget. This was revealed, and after it he forgot nothing.

7.explain: Illā mā shāʾ Allāh: except what Allah wills to remove from memory for a wise reason. He knows al-jahr, what is open, and what is hidden, so He legislates what is best.

8.explain: Nuyassiruka lil-yusrā: We will make the easy way easy for you: good deeds, and a religion and law that are easy and straight.

9.explain: Fa-dhakkir: so remind with the Quran. “If it benefits” either stresses that reminding always helps, or means remind where it helps, not where it only causes harm.

10.explain: Sayadhdhakkaru man yakhshā: whoever fears Allah, knowing he will meet Him, takes the reminder and acts on it.
10.why: Reportedly revealed about Ibn Umm Maktūm.

11.explain: Al-ashqā, the most wretched one, avoids the reminder and pushes it aside.
11.why: Reportedly revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah.

12.explain: He enters an-nār al-kubrā, the great Fire of the Hereafter, far hotter than any fire of this world.

13.explain: He neither dies there and rests, nor lives a life of any benefit. He wishes for death and it never comes.

14.explain: Qad aflaḥa: truly successful is whoever tazakkā, purifies himself from shirk, wrongdoing and bad character.
14.why: Some reports link it to charity paid before the Eid prayer, though the surah is Makkan and there was no Eid then. Other reports link it to ʿUthmān or Abū Bakr.

15.explain: He remembers his Lord’s name, his heart filled with it, and prays. Prayer is the measure of faith. Some apply it to the Eid prayer.

16.explain: Bal tuʾthirūn: but you put this world first, choosing its short, spoiled pleasures, because it is right in front of you and the Hereafter is only described.

17.explain: The Hereafter is khayr, better in everything a person could want, and abqā, lasting forever. This world passes.

18.explain: Hādhā, “this”, either the whole surah or the message of ayat 14–17, was in aṣ-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā, the scriptures sent before the Quran.

19.explain: The scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā. The same call to success and the same warning about this world run through every revealed message.
